jess: Heads-up — after the kernel selection change rolled last night we're seeing a host-side CPU regression concentrated in tokenization + HTTP/gRPC header parsing for streaming paths. +8-12% CPU on p99 decode windows. :frowning:

arjun: Ugh. Do we have flamegraphs or a perf profile yet?

jess: Pushed a short flame to the perf bucket: https://perf.redwood/internal/objs/171800-push. Quick summary — big stacks in http2::decode_headers and Tokenizer::parse_utf8. KV cache hit-rate is steady.

maria: Important detail — batching heuristics switched to smaller target batch size for the new kernel (to reduce tail on GPU). Could be increasing host-side per-request work.

ken: I pulled a pprof: https://pprof.redwood/171800/host_cpu. Key diff: tokenization syscall count up ~2.1x, grpc frame decode smallwrite count up too.

leo: Reproduction: run this load generator with streaming enabled:
```
./loadgen --rate 600 --mode streaming --payload-size 256 --concurrency 32
```
Observe host CPU climb within ~2m.

jess: Quick grep from server logs:
```
[2026-03-18T03:12:10Z] decode_headers 4.9ms -> 12.1ms
[2026-03-18T03:12:10Z] tokenizer.parse_utf8 0.7ms -> 2.2ms
```

arjun: Sounds like more per-frame processing cost. Two hypotheses: (1) kernel change increased op count per token (kernel side), (2) host parsing now pays more due to different framing (smaller chunks -> more header ops).

maria: Also saw KV cache churn for streaming: more KV lookups per request because minibatches are smaller and we lose effective prefix reuse. KV hit-rate unchanged but the number of lookups per second increased. That increases CPU even with same hit-rate.

ken: Can we try the old kernel in a canary with the new batching heuristic disabled? Need to isolate host vs kernel delta.

jess: I spun up a canary with kernel v2.3 (old) + new runtime config toggled to old batch targets. Early numbers: host CPU flat, GPU latency slightly up but within SLOs. So host regression seems correlated with aggressive small-batch heuristic.

leo: Actionable: revert batching target to 64/128-ish for streaming, add a temporary coalescing shim on host that merges tiny frames before header decode.

arjun: For the coalescing shim — can we do it without changing call path heavy? Maybe a small ring-buffer that defers header decode for <= X bytes for up to 10ms.

maria: +1. Also adding instrumentation to count "frames-per-request" and "kv-lookup-per-request" so we can quantify.

sre-bot: deploybot: Rolling canary deploy started for canary-host-3 with kernel=v2.3 + batching=legacy at 1718010200.

jess: Quick perf patch I tried locally: small-frame coalescer reduced http2 decode calls by ~48% on the loadgen. Patch:
```
// coalesce small frames up to 256B or until EOL
if (frame.len <= 256) buffer.append(frame); else decode(frame)
```
That bumped p99 CPU down ~6%.

ken: Nice. We should add microbench for the coalescer path and ensure we don't add latency regressions for low-latency requests. Add a histogram for coalescing delay.

arjun: Also check kernel selection heuristics: the new heuristic was preferring kernels with lower GPU tail but higher per-token preproc cost. We might want a policy that optimizes end-to-end host+gpu cost, not just GPU.

maria: I'll add a metric surface: host_cpu_token_preproc + kernel_selected -> we can build a cost model.

leo: Tentative rollout plan: (1) merge coalescer as opt-in feature flag, (2) revert batching target for streaming while we collect more telemetry, (3) update kernel selection policy to include host-side preprocess cost weight.

jess: TL;DR: regression tracked to batching heuristic + kernel selection combo. Temporary mitigations: enable coalescer + revert new small-batch target for streaming canaries. Next: build host-aware kernel selection and refine batching to preserve KV reuse.

ken: I'll open a short PR for the coalescer with tests and a microbenchmark. Assign to @jess for review.

arjun: I'll start a short cost-model spike to quantify host vs GPU tradeoffs.

maria: Adding the frames-per-request and kv-lookup metrics to the runtime telemetry dashboard now.

jess: Great. Thanks all. Please add any quick findings here. :thumbsup:
